summary: Frontend-only validation of the NEW two-step add-to-thesis flow with dual-score preview in block 1.1b ('Tesis ya generadas que encajan'). End-to-end PASS for ALL scope items. (1) Generated MSFT company thesis via Empresa→Tesis mode, hit dedup-warning, clicked 'Reescribir igualmente' → thesis-result appeared after ~40s. (2) Block 1.1b 'existing-matches' rendered. (3) Clicked 'Calcular score' (data-testid matched-thesis-eval-thesis_test_aidc) → 'Calculando score…' indicator shown immediately → preview appeared in ~11s with BOTH numeric values: preview-overall-thesis_test_aidc='74' and preview-tam-thesis_test_aidc='0.71'. (4) 'Cancelar' (matched-thesis-cancel-thesis_test_aidc) works: clicking it hides the preview (count→0); re-clicking 'Calcular score' re-evaluates and re-shows preview. (5) 'Confirmar · Añadir MSFT' (matched-thesis-add-thesis_test_aidc) completed in 4.0s (FAST, reusing prior evaluation — well under the 30s LLM path). Toast 'MSFT añadida a "IA y centros de datos"' shown. Row disappeared after success. (6) Sidebar refresh (refresh-data-btn) updated MSFT toggle from '0 TESIS' → '1 TESIS' and dropdown lists 'IA y centros de datos' as included.

ui_bugs.issue: Duplicate matched-thesis rows for the same thesis_id. When the LLM rewrite of MSFT produces two trends that both map to thesis_test_aidc, the backend's link-suggestions returns the same matched thesis twice and the UI renders TWO identical rows (verified: 2 instances of [data-testid=matched-thesis-thesis_test_aidc] and 2 of [data-testid=matched-thesis-eval-thesis_test_aidc] in the DOM). React also logs 'Encountered two children with the same key: thesis_test_aidc'. Functionality still works (clicking either yields the correct flow) but the testids become non-unique (strict mode violations in tests) and the user sees two redundant rows.

action_items: Dedupe existing-matches by thesis_id before rendering in ThesisResult.jsx (e.g. const matches = uniqBy(linkData?.to_add?.filter(m=>!m.already_in), 'thesis_id')). This will also fix the React duplicate-key warning emitted on every render of this block.
critical_code_review_comments: ThesisResult.jsx — existing-matches rendering does not deduplicate by thesis_id. Backend /thesis/{id}/link-suggestions can legitimately return the same matched thesis multiple times (one per matching trend in the company thesis), but the UI should aggregate to a single row per thesis. Currently uses thesis_id as React key with duplicates, producing the key collision warning.

ThesisResult.jsx — Re-clicking 'Calcular score' after Cancelar makes a fresh LLM call (~15s) rather than caching the previously computed evaluation in component state. Consider memoizing the last preview keyed by ticker so a Cancel→re-Calcular is instantaneous within the same session.
seed_data_creation: Re-ran /app/backend/tests/seed_company_thesis_test.py to reset MSFT's company-thesis seed. IMPORTANT: that seed alone does NOT remove MSFT from thesis_test_aidc.companies (a previous test run had added MSFT). I manually removed it via a direct MongoDB update: db.theses.update_one({'id':'thesis_test_aidc'}, {$pull: {companies: {ticker:'MSFT'}}}) so the existing-matches block would render the 'Calcular score' button. After this test run, MSFT is again a member of thesis_test_aidc — re-run the same pull to reset before retesting.

Block 1.2 'Nuevas tesis sugeridas' was empty on this run (all rewritten trends matched existing theses) — UI correctly shows the empty-state message.
rca of the issue: DUPLICATE ROW BUG: When generating a company thesis (e.g. MSFT) that has multiple trends mapping to the same existing user thesis (e.g. thesis_test_aidc), POST /thesis/{id}/link-suggestions returns one entry per (company_trend, matched_thesis) pair without deduplicating by thesis_id. The frontend's existingMatches.map() then renders one MatchedThesisRow per entry using thesis_id as the React key, producing both visual duplicates and a React 'duplicate key' console error. Mitigation: dedupe in ThesisResult.jsx by thesis_id (keep highest similarity / first occurrence) OR fix in the backend route to group matches per thesis_id.
